investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Blocked by Swarm Agent Quota Exhaustion (HTTP 409)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-15T17:10:43–47Z with an identical HTTP 409 response from POST /api/agents: the swarm backend rejected the creation request because the agent quota limit of 100 has been reached. Because the failure occurs at the agent creation step shared by all three checks, no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was ever collected, causing a complete contract gap for the remote-agent-create eval.
investigation.rootCause: The production swarm backend is returning HTTP 409 conflict with the message "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100" on every POST /api/agents call made by the eval runner. This prevents the eval from creating a remote agent at all, so the runner never reaches the VM-readiness or state-polling steps, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-create (requiring orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) is entirely unmet. The failure is localized to the POST /api/agents endpoint in the production-api runtime environment and is an eval-infrastructure signal against the production API; no user-traffic or incident evidence is present in the packet to confirm a broader user-facing outage.
proof: failed-check.message: POST /api/agents failed with 409 — error body contains 'conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100', confirming the swarm backend rejected the creation request due to quota exhaustion.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}), confirming the runner never progressed past the creation call and collected zero contract fields.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are missing, consistent with the probe aborting at the createAgent call before any evidence could be written.

sibling.remote-agent-state and sibling.remote-agent-runtime: both siblings carry the identical 409 message and empty evidence, confirming the shared createAgent dependency failed for every check in the feature.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:104-112 (expected-output-contract): contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready], neither of which can be asserted when agent creation fails.
verifierContext.siblingCorrelation.likelySharedDependencyFailure: true — verifier independently flagged a shared upstream dependency failure across all three remote-agents checks.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — Swarm agent quota at hard limit: the production swarm backend enforces a per-org (or global) limit of 100 agents and that limit is currently reached, causing every new POST /api/agents to return 409. This is directly stated in the error body (evidence: failed-check.message).

SECONDARY — Leaked or un-cleaned eval agents from prior runs: the eval runner uses a withCleanup wrapper (source-context run-status-probes.mjs:806) to delete agents after each run. If a previous run crashed before cleanup, orphaned eval agents may be accumulating against the quota, eventually exhausting it.

TERTIARY — Quota limit misconfiguration or reduction: the hard limit of 100 may have been lowered by a backend configuration change, causing previously-passing runs to now exceed the threshold. No prior passing run history exists in the packet (verifierContext.history.lastPassingAt: null) so this cannot be confirmed or ruled out from available evidence.

LOW CONFIDENCE — Commit 57b077e as a contributing factor: this commit touched .github/workflows/aura-observability.yml and aura-evals.yml (suspect-change.57b077e), which could have altered eval scheduling frequency or parallelism, potentially increasing the rate of agent creation and quota consumption. However, the commit's candidateTouchedPaths list is empty and no eval-runner or API source files are confirmed changed, so this remains a low-confidence hypothesis only.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Creation Blocked by Swarm Agent Quota Exhaustion (HTTP 409)
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-15T17:10:43–47Z with an identical HTTP 409 response from POST /api/agents: the swarm backend rejected the creation request because the agent quota limit of 100 has been reached. Because the failure occurs at the agent creation step shared by all three checks, no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was ever collected, causing a complete contract gap for the remote-agent-create eval.
investigations.rootCause: The production swarm backend is returning HTTP 409 conflict with the message "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100" on every POST /api/agents call made by the eval runner. This prevents the eval from creating a remote agent at all, so the runner never reaches the VM-readiness or state-polling steps, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-create (requiring orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) is entirely unmet. The failure is localized to the POST /api/agents endpoint in the production-api runtime environment and is an eval-infrastructure signal against the production API; no user-traffic or incident evidence is present in the packet to confirm a broader user-facing outage.
proof: failed-check.message: POST /api/agents failed with 409 — error body contains 'conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100', confirming the swarm backend rejected the creation request due to quota exhaustion.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}), confirming the runner never progressed past the creation call and collected zero contract fields.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are missing, consistent with the probe aborting at the createAgent call before any evidence could be written.

sibling.remote-agent-state and sibling.remote-agent-runtime: both siblings carry the identical 409 message and empty evidence, confirming the shared createAgent dependency failed for every check in the feature.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:800-808 (eval-runner-branch): runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 808 immediately after resolving orgId — the 409 from this call is the earliest failure boundary.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:104-112 (expected-output-contract): contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready], neither of which can be asserted when agent creation fails.
verifierContext.siblingCorrelation.likelySharedDependencyFailure: true — verifier independently flagged a shared upstream dependency failure across all three remote-agents checks.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — Swarm agent quota at hard limit: the production swarm backend enforces a per-org (or global) limit of 100 agents and that limit is currently reached, causing every new POST /api/agents to return 409. This is directly stated in the error body (evidence: failed-check.message).

SECONDARY — Leaked or un-cleaned eval agents from prior runs: the eval runner uses a withCleanup wrapper (source-context run-status-probes.mjs:806) to delete agents after each run. If a previous run crashed before cleanup, orphaned eval agents may be accumulating against the quota, eventually exhausting it.

TERTIARY — Quota limit misconfiguration or reduction: the hard limit of 100 may have been lowered by a backend configuration change, causing previously-passing runs to now exceed the threshold. No prior passing run history exists in the packet (verifierContext.history.lastPassingAt: null) so this cannot be confirmed or ruled out from available evidence.

LOW CONFIDENCE — Commit 57b077e as a contributing factor: this commit touched .github/workflows/aura-observability.yml and aura-evals.yml (suspect-change.57b077e), which could have altered eval scheduling frequency or parallelism, potentially increasing the rate of agent creation and quota consumption. However, the commit's candidateTouchedPaths list is empty and no eval-runner or API source files are confirmed changed, so this remains a low-confidence hypothesis only.
